enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
450 AM MDT Sat Oct 31 2026

...New UPDATE, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...



.UPDATE...
Issued at 437 AM MDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Moisture left over from recent rains, light winds, and cooler
temperatures will set up saturated atmospheric conditions and 
generate very low cloud decks and patchy fog this morning. 
Visibilities will vary, but may get a low as a mile. Fog will
begin to dissipate around mid morning. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES... Updated at 923 AM MDT Thu Oct 29 2026

 - Patchy morning fog may reduce visibilities down to 1 mile 

 - Halloween will feature mostly dry conditions, light winds, and
   seasonal temperatures. 

 - A upper level system will bring more showers and thunderstorms to 
   the area Sunday afternoon into Monday morning.

 - Quieter and drier weather will prevail after Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1029 PM MDT Fri Oct 30 2026

Batch of showers working west to east but should fizzle away by 
sunrise. Some lingering showery debris possible Saturday morning. 
Anomalous moisture will still be overhead with a focus on 
locations along the Int'l Border. Lower PW values over the 
northern half of the CONUS (0.7"-0.8") and higher values down 
south (0.9"-1.1"). Expect mostly cloudy skies Saturday. No real 
forcing for storms on Saturday, even though we have the moisture. 
If there's any breaks in the clouds, maybe a shower or 
thunderstorm possible. HRRR is suggesting some type of activity 
generally Deming and west. Halloween does look like it'll feature 
good weather for many locations. Highs will reach to the low to 
mid 70s but will dip into the 60s after dark. Winds stay light 
through the day and evening.

The next round of showers and thunderstorms exists Sunday evening. A 
southern Pacific low will meet up with a more northern Pacific low, 
joining up over the desert SW. Moisture is still well above normal 
with PW values of 0.9"-1.1". Now this time, we will have synoptic 
level forcing for storms Sunday evening. Uncertain how much 
instability there will be. GFS suggests very low CAPE values, but 
the EC suggest CAPEs of 500-1000 J/kg. After further digging, the 
NBM and LREF has more modest CAPE values (LREF ~500 J/kg, NBM ~600-
1000 J/kg) with a focus over Hudspeth  and S. Otero counties. 
However, this area of instability may not be influenced just yet but 
the synoptic forcing. One thing we will have plenty of is shear. 
Will also have a pacific cold front moving through with this trough 
late Sunday and into Monday. May just have more showery activity 
with embedded thunderstorms that evening. Rain chances will push 
eastward through the overnight with some lingering showery activity 
possible Monday morning and afternoon. In addition to rain chances, 
winds will be breezy Sunday afternoon at 15-25 mph with gusts to 40 
mph. 

By Monday afternoon, the center of the low will cross northern NM, 
sweeping out any moisture leftover. Winds will continue to be breezy 
Monday afternoon with similar wind speeds to Sunday. A much needed 
stretch of dry weather is ahead Tuesday through at least Friday.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 437 AM MDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Bulk of the showery activity has pushed east of the terminals. 
Saturated atmospheric conditions with light winds and low cloud 
decks will generate patchy fog that could intermittently lower 
visibilities down 1 to 4 miles at terminals. In addition, moist 
conditions will set up very low cloud decks below a 1000 feet 
along with the patchy fog. Clouds should lift and fog dissipate 
before 18Z mid day. Drier conditions will prevail afterwards. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 437 AM MDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Rain has largely ended in the area, but moist conditions, low
clouds, and light winds will generate patchy fog this morning that
will will lower visibilities down to a mile or less in some
locations. Moist conditions will keep fire weather concerns low. 
Min RHs today will be no less than 45% for most of the region, and
Saturday's min RHs will be quite similar, even with a lull in the
rain. Another round of rain will sweep through on Sunday 
afternoon as a second trough moves through. Dry conditions return 
Monday afternoon. Ventilation rates will improve from Poor today 
to Very Good on Sunday.

&&
